correctness.rationale: At every degree-two subdivision vertex, its two original neighbours must have distinct colors, and a proper three-coloring forces the third color. Hence each used color class in the opposite original part must have odd size at every original vertex. Counting one/two odd classes gives the asserted parity-specific optimum and exact three-color counts; a two-color checkerboard on subdivisions gives the even-even four-color construction. For p=2, each page has exactly six valid triples given hub colors. Enforcing both parity and used support at both hubs (rather than parity alone) yields the stated all-even-q signed character enumeration; the zero case q even-even follows from the rigid three-color obstruction.
risks: The four-color exact census is proved only for p=2 and positive even q, not for all even-even p,q; finite computations cannot justify the general q formula without the character argument.

value.rationale: The once-subdivided complete bipartite family is the natural edge-incidence graph of K_{p,q}; parity of the two original sides is an intrinsic structural parameter. Determining its exact chromatic threshold for every side size and a full all-q labelled optimum count for the natural two-hub multitheta family is a motivated classification, not a parameter rename or small-case counting exercise.
risks: The all-even-even four-color census for p>2 remains open; the result should not be represented as its solution.
